description.value: A real-time fMRI neurofeedback study testing whether feedback from left LPFC activity enhances cognitive reappraisal and reduces amygdala activation.

spans.text: This feasibility study focused on the facilitative effect of fMRI feedback on a putative brain network for voluntary emotion regulation.

In each continuous run, 441 volumes were acquired (TR = 1500 ms) with 26 axial slices in ascending order (thickness 2.5 mm, 0.5 mm gap) and 3-mm in-plane resolution, ensuring full coverage of the prefrontal, limbic and visual areas with limited coverage of high parietal cortices and the cerebellum , as a trade-off between adequate spatial coverage and imaging speed.

spans.text: Preprocessing of imaging data and statistical analysis were carried out using BrainVoyager QX 2.4.0 (Brain Innovation, Maastricht, The Netherlands).

description.value: Preprocessing included slice scan time correction, motion correction, high-pass filtering, spatial smoothing, anatomical intensity correction, alignment and transformation to Talairach space.

spans.text: Preprocessing of the data included slice scan time correction, 3D motion detection and correction with rigid body transformations, high-pass filtering to remove low-frequency drifts using a GLM approach with a Fourier basis set (5 sine/cosine cycles) and spatial smoothing with a Gaussian kernel with bandwidth of 6 mm. The acquired anatomical 3D data sets were corrected for spatial intensity inhomogeneities. The functional volumes were then aligned with the corresponding anatomical data sets. Each 3D dataset was subsequently transformed into standard Talairach space to allow for group analysis.

instructions.value: During view blocks, participants watched the aversive images and counted backwards from 900. During regulate blocks, they applied an appropriate cognitive reappraisal strategy to each image to reduce negative emotions. Feedback-group participants were asked to keep left LPFC ROI activation as high as possible using cognitive reappraisal strategies; control participants were asked to make their best effort to decrease negative emotions using cognitive reappraisal.
